Hi Jennifer — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the technical options below; attaching a tiny redacted snippet (traceid-sample-snippet.txt) and a one-pager explaining the default behaviors (redwood-log-policy-onepager.pdf).

Summary of capabilities (short):
- Default behavior: we capture structured request/response logs (headers, metadata, sizes, latencies) and a sampling of bodies for debugging. Body capture is off by default for PII-protected endpoints; it must be enabled or configured per route.
- Headers: personal or sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email) are masked by default in hosted deployments. Customers can specify additional header keys to mask.
- Trace IDs: three configurable modes at ingest:
  1) passthrough: store trace IDs as-is (for customers that need exact end-to-end correlation)
  2) deterministic-hash: we run a one-way SHA-256 hash (or HMAC with customer key) on trace IDs; stored value is non-reversible and consistent for correlation
  3) mapping: we map incoming trace IDs to internal UUIDs and keep the mapping for the configured retention window (mapping is reversible while mapping exists)
- Redaction at field-level: request/response JSON paths can be redacted via config (replace with [REDACTED]) or pseudonymized (replace with stable token).
- Retention: per-tenant, per-logstream retention policies. Example presets: 7 days (dev), 90 days (default), 3 years (archival); headers-only retention can be set separately from bodies.
- Regional residency: logs can be stored in a single region (us-west-2 or us-east-1) for Private deployments; hosted customers may request region-specific retention under contract.
- Export: we can generate redacted log bundles for audits; bundles include a short manifest describing masking rules applied.

Acceptance criteria suggestions for POC:
- We will provide a redacted bundle (sample) within 24 hours so Greenfield can validate masking approach.
- Greenfield will provide 2 example trace IDs and 3 example request payloads to validate deterministic-hash vs mapping behavior.
- Agreement on retention windows (headers vs bodies) for the POC and on-region storage.

Quick note on security: deterministic hashing can be HMACed with a customer-provided key (so values are non-reversible by Redwood if requested). Mapping mode requires secure mapping store; we recommend mapping only for short-term debug workflows.

Let us know which mode you'd like to test and we will generate the sample bundle.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform
